question:
A 13-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of worsening fever, headache, photophobia, and nausea for 2 days. One week ago, she returned from summer camp. She has received all age-appropriate immunizations. Her temperature is 39.1°C (102.3°F). She is oriented to person, place, and time. Physical examination shows a maculopapular rash. There is rigidity of the neck; forced flexion of the neck results in involuntary flexion of the knees and hips. Cerebrospinal fluid studies show:
Opening pressure 120 mm H2O
Appearance Clear
Protein 47 mg/dL
Glucose 68 mg/dL
White cell count 280/mm3
Segmented neutrophils 15%
Lymphocytes 85%
Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "13-year-old girl with fever and headache" -> "recent summer camp exposure" -> "possible viral or bacterial infection" -> "maculopapular rash present" -> "neck rigidity and positive Brudzinski's sign" -> "suggestive of meningitis" -> "CSF shows elevated white cell count with lymphocytic predominance" -> "indicates viral etiology" -> "Echovirus is a common cause of viral meningitis in children" -> 85%

CHAIN: "13-year-old girl with fever and headache" -> "recent summer camp exposure" -> "possible viral or bacterial infection" -> "maculopapular rash present" -> "neck rigidity and positive Brudzinski's sign" -> "suggestive of meningitis" -> "CSF shows elevated white cell count with lymphocytic predominance" -> "bacterial meningitis less likely due to lymphocyte predominance" -> "Herpes simplex virus can cause viral meningitis" -> "but less common in this age group" -> "Echovirus is more prevalent in this scenario" -> 80%

CHAIN: "13-year-old girl with fever and headache" -> "recent summer camp exposure" -> "possible viral or bacterial infection" -> "maculopapular rash present" -> "neck rigidity and positive Brudzinski's sign" -> "suggestive of meningitis" -> "CSF shows elevated white cell count with lymphocytic predominance" -> "bacterial meningitis less likely due to lymphocyte predominance" -> "Listeria monocytogenes typically affects older adults" -> "Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria meningitidis are less likely due to CSF findings" -> "Echovirus is a common cause of viral meningitis in children" -> 90%
analysis: The clinical presentation of fever, headache, photophobia, nausea, and neck rigidity, along with the CSF findings of elevated white blood cell count with a predominance of lymphocytes, normal glucose levels, and mildly elevated protein, suggests viral meningitis. The most common viral cause in this age group, especially after recent camp exposure, is Echovirus, which is a member of the enterovirus family. Other options like Listeria monocytogenes and Streptococcus pneumoniae typically present with neutrophilic pleocytosis and lower glucose levels, while Herpes simplex virus would likely show more severe symptoms and possibly a different CSF profile. Neisseria meningitidis would also present with neutrophilic pleocytosis. Therefore, the most likely causal organism is Echovirus.
